productDecision: Defer Command Window out of the current authored wave rather than cycling through named bosses until one happens not to collide. The Glukhar/Reserve form is a semantic subset of vanilla Payback, and the remaining obvious boss/follower substitutions still express the same generic boss-kill gameplay already represented heavily by vanilla. A future Command Window may return only with a genuinely distinct command-disruption mechanic backed by exact SPT 4.1.3 condition authority. No replacement or filler operation is required.
whyNoImmediateRetarget: Changing only the boss name does not change the gameplay problem; it remains a bounded named-boss kill followed by extraction.
The curation policy explicitly rejects quota-filling and literal or semantic vanilla duplication.
The active wave already contains specialist contact, interdiction, precision and critical-access operations, so campaign structure does not require an artificial boss slot.
The previous critical reward envelope is removed with the deferred operation rather than reassigned to unrelated content.

relevantShape: survive and extract from Reserve through Cliff Descent
vanilla.reason: The rejected Admiral form asks for the same named command target on the same map followed by extraction. Retargeting to another named boss without a new mechanic would preserve the generic boss-contract problem rather than solve it.

economyReview.reason: A bounded reward did not rescue a duplicate objective. The reward allocation is removed from the active envelope and is not transferred to another operation.

rejectedAlternatives: Glukhar on Reserve plus successful extraction because vanilla Payback is a semantic superset
swapping Glukhar for another named boss while keeping the same generic kill-and-extract mechanic
keeping or replacing the operation only to preserve authored quest count
